ids.change: Admission closes before an ordered shutdown sentinel. Full backlog cannot lose the sentinel silently. Shared shutdown task is shielded against caller cancellation. Batch rollback, terminal accounting, in-memory failed transactions and an exception expose failure instead of clean shutdown. Queue-full admission raises. Initialization is owned by a shielded task; close waits for it and closes the returned connection. Simultaneous initialize is rejected; cancelling initialize starts shared cleanup and cannot reopen admission.
limits: Auxiliary queue only, not canonical ledger actor. Submission confirms admission only; normal shutdown confirms commits within SQLite contract.
Failed batch/backlog is retained in memory for caller recovery, not durable recovery storage; failed COMMIT can have an unknown outcome and retry must inspect the database.
No power-cut test or multi-event-loop/thread sharing guarantee.

ids.change: Every domain checks enqueue acceptance before appending report receipt; False raises. Worker exceptions propagate. Successful report labels persistence QUEUED_NOT_CONFIRMED.
limits: True enqueue is not a durability acknowledgement. No cross-domain all-or-nothing commit. Earlier accepted receipts can remain queued when a later domain fails.
Producer/ledger/attester boundaries in targeted tests use in-memory recorders and synthetic receipts, without starting a real cold-ledger actor or hardware query.

ids.change: BEGIN IMMEDIATE re-reads the committed tip and chooses the current predecessor/logical tick before hash and INSERT. Missing tracking ID cannot be called replay. Tracking IDs use UUID to avoid same-second cross-instance collisions; input JSON is copied. Invalid, stopped or full admission is explicit, and stop drains accepted backlog. Cancellation of the processing loop now propagates, rather than returning normal completion for an unpersisted extracted claim.
limits: Tracking is admission, not per-claim durability acknowledgement; the state-loop task must be observed for processing failures.
Actual SQLite/WAL fixtures cover two concurrent instances, restart and chain linkage; no physical power-cut or hostile database-file replacement test.
Existing fail-stop process termination on catastrophic database error remains; test fixture replaces os.kill to prevent any process termination.

ids.change: Scheduler owns explicit tasks and shields the gather. On any exception/caller cancellation, it cancels and awaits all tasks under ThermalLock; repeated parent cancellation cannot interrupt the shared cleanup and free the lock early.
limits: Cancellation-resistant tasks may keep the lock held indefinitely; no claim of forced termination.
Filesystem lock scope/identity/permissions are unchanged, outside this finding. Tests exercise cooperative tasks and real temporary lock paths.

limits: Node VM executes the actual Worker module with only postal-mime dependency and platform boundaries injected. No SMTP delivery, Cloudflare deployment or real webhook was performed.
Handler failure is observable; platform redelivery, durable queue retention and exactly-once webhook delivery are not guaranteed.
